segments.title: Force K as a heavy raider-hunting force
segments.summary: In 1939, Force K combined HMS Renown, HMS Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers as a heavy anti-surface raider-hunting group.
segments.body: Force K carried unusually heavy striking power for hunting enemy surface raiders. Its main ships were the battlecruiser HMS Renown and the aircraft carrier HMS Ark Royal, supported by H-class destroyers. Together they provided carrier aircraft, heavy guns, speed, and a destroyer screen in one group. The combination explains why Force K could respond to distant surface-raider threats.

evidence.note: The transcript calls Force K a heavy anti-surface force and names Renown, Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers.

segments.title: Reinforcing the River Plate hunt from Freetown
segments.summary: During the Battle of the River Plate crisis, Force K raced from Freetown to reinforce Harwood's squadron if Admiral Graf Spee broke out.
segments.body: The Battle of the River Plate shows why the Royal Navy based Force K at Freetown. The group raced across the Atlantic to reinforce Commodore Harwood's squadron with heavier ships if Admiral Graf Spee attempted to break out. Freetown, rather than Gibraltar, was Force K's operating area. The deployment placed a powerful mobile force where it could help close an escape route beyond the cruisers already in contact.

evidence.note: Dr. Clarke describes Force K crossing from Freetown to support Harwood against a Graf Spee breakout.

segments.title: A layered trap for a South Atlantic raider
segments.summary: Ark Royal's Swordfish, radio signals, and Renown's speed and guns formed a layered response to a surface raider returning north.
segments.body: Force K combined reconnaissance, carrier aviation, speed, and surface gun power. Radio signals could narrow the search as a German surface raider tried to pass from the South Atlantic into the North Atlantic. Ark Royal's Swordfish could locate and attack it, perhaps slowing it or sinking it. If the ship survived, Renown's speed and guns provided the final interception. Together, those naval capabilities could stop a raider from returning north.

evidence.note: The transcript links Ark Royal aircraft, Renown, radio signals, Swordfish attacks, and the interception of a raider moving from the South to North Atlantic.

segments.title: How Force K changed after 1939
segments.summary: Force K referred to different formations in 1939, 1940, and 1942, so the date determines which ships and mission the name identifies.
segments.body: Force K referred to several different wartime formations. The 1939 group combined Renown, Ark Royal, and H-class destroyers, while later groups with the same name had different ships and roles. The closing comparison describes the 1942 Force K as a surface-raiding force. The date therefore matters whenever Force K appears in an account.

evidence.note: The transcript distinguishes Force K in 1939 from later 1940 and 1942 formations and calls the 1942 force the surface raiders.
